summary: Sally McAra specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), supervised by Christine Dureau and Karen Nero from circa 1998 to 2000.
Sally Mellick Cutler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford by 1993 and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office.

Salomon Lefmann (1831–1912) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (~1859–1861) and held the Extraordinariat für Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (~1866–1912).

Sam Harris is a philosopher who studied at Stanford University (~1997–2000) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2009). His teachers include Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.

Sam van Schaik works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Manchester (~1995–2000), he studied under teachers including Lama Jampa Thaye and managed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (~2002–2019).
Samani Pratibha Pragya works in religious studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (~2008–2013), where she also served as a research assistant.

Samdhong Rinpoche is a Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries. He served as Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1971–1977) and Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1985–1987).

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar educated at Drepung Monastery, SOAS, and the University of London under David L. Snellgrove. He held posts at SOAS, Collège de France, CNRS, and Paris Nanterre University.

Samuel Beal (1825–1889) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. After earning his B.A. at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1843–1847), he served as Professor of Chinese at University College London (~1877–1889).

Samuel M. Grupper specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University by circa 1980 under committee members including Denis Sinor and Helmut Hoffmann.
Sandra Bell is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and held an academic post there.
Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she was supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes and taught by Anne MacDonald.

Sandra Smets is a scholar in the field of Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under supervisor Christophe Vielle, alongside committee members Jean-Marie Verpoorten, Éric Pirart, Jean-Michel Delire, and Gérard Colas.
Sang-Kyun Sun works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under the supervision of Sanghasen Singh and has served as a lecturer at JinGak Sangha College.

Sangay Dorji is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tengtho Monastery and Simtokha Dzong, he taught at Simtokha Dzong and served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission (~1999).
Sangharakshita (1925–2018) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher C. M. Chen from circa 1950 to 1964 and founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1968.

Sangseraima Ujeed works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2018) and held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2019–2021).
Sangye Tenzin (1912–1977) was a scholar in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery and served as the Abbot of Menri Monastery.

Sanjay Subrahmanyam is a historian who studied at the University of Delhi and Delhi School of Economics (~1980–1987). He has held posts at EHESS (~1995–2002), Oxford (~2002–2004), UCLA (~2004), and Collège de France (~2013–2021).
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He was guided and taught by Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya and studied under traditional teacher A. P. Lama.
